# v1.8.2 — reliability

Operational and presentation fixes after the failed daily refresh of 12 October 2026. Nothing in the figures or the legal text changes.

- **Daily refresh close to 06:00 UTC.** GitHub had been starting the scheduled refresh five to eight hours late. An hourly check now starts the day's refresh at the first check at or after 06:00 UTC, retries a failed download at the next hour (up to six attempts a day), and still contacts CelesTrak and GCAT only for that daily pull.
- **Honest timing.** The header and the Provenance panel give the time each snapshot was actually fetched, instead of a fixed "06:00Z".
- **Snapshot date on small screens.** Phones and tablets now show the snapshot date and fetch time, which every citation depends on.
- **Alerts.** A failed refresh still opens an issue, and the next successful refresh now closes it. The companion archive raises an issue if the live snapshot is ever more than 30 hours old.
- **Archive.** Every published snapshot is archived within the hour, never replaced, and listed with its SHA-256 checksum.
- **Build.** The QA gate runs on Node 24 with current GitHub Actions, and waits on conditions instead of fixed delays.

Full details: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/hallamburnapp-cloud/stars-observatory/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
